newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Issue Dept assets fall to 3.117 bln marks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Issue Dept assets fall to 3.117 bln marks.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) Issue Department assets and liabilities fell to 3.117 billion marks ($1.7 billion) on July 25 from 3.196 billion marks a week earlier, the BNB said on Monday.
BNB officials were not immedately available for comment on the reasons for the fall.

The lev was pegged at 1,000 levs to the mark, which is an anchor currency under an IMF-prescribed currency board system. A currency board system is a fixed-exchange rate mechanism introduced on July 1 to boost confidence in the lev.
The system requires levs in circulation to be matched by Issue Department assets and bans the BNB from lending to the government and banks.
The Issue Department publishes its balance sheet weekly on BNB contributor pages.
The cash and nostro and vostro accounts in foreign currencies of the assets rose to the mark equivalent of 1.432 trillion levs on July 25 from 1.391 trillion levs ($756 million) on July 18.
The BNB holdings in foreign securities fell to the equivalent of 1.04 trillion levs from 1.16 trillion levs last week.

Apart from the BNB holdings in foreign securities and cash and nostro accounts in foreign currencies, the Issue Department assets also included 640.7 billion levs in monetary gold and 3.7 billion levs in accrued interest receivable on July 25.
Currency in circulation, a part of Issue Department liabilities rose to 806.3 billion levs on July 25 from 774.1 billion levs a week earlier.

The department's liabilities also included 727.7 billion levs in bank deposits and current accounts, 432.5 billion levs in government deposits and accounts and 602.3 billion levs in the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development account.
Part of the liabilities also were 8.83 billion levs in other deposits and accrued interest payable of 336 million levs.
The liabilities also included a 538.7 billion lev deposit of the BNB Banking Department that can be lent to sound banks only in case of systemic risk for the banking and payments system.

The Banking Department's primary objective is to ensure confidence in the liquidity of the banking system and more broadly, the efficiency in key financial markets. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145 ($ = 1.842 German Marks) ($ = 1840 Bulgarian Levs)
